author: Michal238
text:
Hi everyone

I'm happy to be back and thank you IF for putting me on the list.

I decided to start a new journal here, but this time it will be more
results oriented. I'm going to post my statements regularly regardless
of how good/bad it is. The reason for that is that I want to be honest
about my performance in order to not create unrealistic expectations for
 new members - that can happen when winning trades are posted (mostly)
and great setups explained. It all looks logical and easy in hindsight
but even though I have a good understanding, in real time I have doubts
all the time and it is difficult to make a good decision.

So I'm going to talk about ways/techniques I will use to improve my
performance and whether it worked or not, and if I managed to apply it
correctly. I am also going to post a lot of setups with detailed
explanations and commentary, as I used to in my old journal.

Here goes my first statement. I started trading this account 25th of
January - it is demo, because there is a lot of things I can improve,
and losing a lot of real money had a really bad effect on my psyche and I
 had to take a break from trading... Trading live is no time for
improvements - all bad habits can be changed while trading on demo and
that is what I intend to do. I will continue this until I can see
consistent results on weekly basis for the period of 2 months at least.

The number of trades is much higher than a number of setups I traded. It
 is something I need to work on - I enjoy too much pressing these
buttons. Also, there is a ton of breakeven/small loss/small profit
trades - this is where I make an impulsive decision, or bad decision and
 realize it - then I close trades to avoid further losses. Overtrading
is something I struggle with for a long time now, also respecting
trading rules etc.

I don't know if there is a hope in trading career for people like me,
but I'm not going to give up... I think that I slightly improve over
time even though I'm nowhere near to overcoming all psychological
challenges of trading. The current result may seem pretty decent right
now but the real challenge will come when I'll have next losing streak. I
 had one already - I survived, but suffered 10% drawdown. It was
basically 2 setups where I entered too many times breaking MM rules.
Another big issue is entering after a reaction to a level - RR is worse
and bounce already happened - pointless. I'll work on that as well and
I'll post updates on my progress in this journal.

Where do I look for trades?

What I aim to do is to take touch trades in the direction of the trend.
But by trend, I mean situation when the price is coming from a valid
zone and didn't reach the target yet. I basically try to find places for
 a touch trade after continuation engulfs. I do this when ITs have
positions open and add on retraces by stopping traders out. When I see
that price is reacting to valid target and there is some kind of
reversal I assume ITs are short (for example) and then I look for
opportunities to join the move. So even though most of my trades can be
classified as continuation trades, all of them are reversal trades at
the same time - because if I sell, I sell against strong (usually)
bullish move on smaller scale, and vice versa.

It is important to analyze all scales and to make sure that you are not
trading against direction signaled by engulf on a higher scale.

I'll quickly mark EUR/USD charts to show what I mean:

This quasimodo is beautiful you can see how clever ITs are. Look how
long price was going up. As price moves up more and more people are
biased long and then big push happens. The way I think about this is as
follows: ITs don't have to do much here. People are biased long and ITs
"add fuel to the fire" to make the move look strong/scary/exciting,
whatever. The point is that now price is where they want to sell at and
people keep buying this thinking that price will go up forever . Btw. there is a big daily "marubozu" candle after pin bar - some people consider this an excellent buy signal.

Countertrend moves are usually strong and it may be counter-intuitive to
 trade against but that is what we do. Here is nice examples of moves
like that. I marked them with arrows. Red lines show where people got
stopped out recently. So I think that ITs are still short and there is
potential for continuation as there is a lot of space below.

Of course, it is easy to mark this stuff in hindsight - much harder to
do it real time because it often seems that move is genuine and it will
stop you out, but you need to pay attention to bigger picture and trade
against moves like these fearlessly.

text:

I know that very well too...

It's the same for me and for hundreds of other traders, I guess...

Let's try to focus on patience, on picking just " The One " screaming to us to be traded.

I very appreciate your idea to show your progress, not hiding any mistake, if given.

I quite agree with you: after the facts we are all GURUs.

Let's see forwards testing.

There is no rush at all.

It all depends on how fast you want to grow.

I personally like to have a kind of "growth plan" in my mind, but just
for understanding that we do not need any greed at all to may have
excellent results.

You perhaps tried that too, but I made a very easy excel sheet to may
see, how many pips daily in profit I would need, to may grow 10% x
month, given a Max SL of 40 pips per trade, and being those 40 pips 2%
of my balance.

Do you want to know how many pips we would need per day (in 20 trading days/month) to achieve that 10% ?

12,5 !

Yes, not even 13 pips a day in profit, applying the easiest possible
compound at the beginning of each new month, and in 9 months your
starting balance is doubled...

So what stress ?

We don't need.

I also made some demo trading for me too, trying to work on patience.

This is the result from the 1st December till 12th February.

If I can do this... you with your reading can do much more.

I know it !

I will now start with a live account again and would like to do like you: to show all, mistakes and achieved targets.

Nothing to hide.

That's the way for a good growth.

Professional and Personal.

As I love to remember to myself sometimes:

" A Black Belt is nothing else than a White Belt, that never stopped getting up once again "

Please forgive my long post in your journal, won't happen again, but I
was glad to read that you will be active here again, as I have always

Dziekuje

author: TheBeard
text:
Always believe in yourself dude.

I have the following thoughts about trading.

Trading forex is an investment product. Investments are usually a form of saving. They're not usually relied on as income.

Making investments for others is a career/job. Careers/jobs for the most part have a salary which you can live off.

So in my mind trading won't be a career for me unless I can trade on other peoples behalf.

Numbers wise If I can make 10% a month, consistently, I'd need a £30k
account to make withdrawls from and another account to compound as
savings. That is a very, very long way away.

I too suffer from frequency of trading. I look back and say to myself "no way was there 50 good setups last week, no way".

Then I tell myself "forex isn't meant to be fun". I even started a
hashtag. A lot of these social media groups with traders in are all so
excited. Saying things like "who's shorting Euro with me" like it's a
team game. It's a game to them. This isn't a game. Not when you truly
want to make it a success.

Another thing I'm doing is meditating. I've not done it for over a week
but starting tomorrow I'm going to start meditating again. This helps me
 with patience.

I opened a live account with £100. Managed to get to £113 pretty quick
tbh then fucked it all the way down to like £56 or something in couple
days. It's now back up to £90 after couple weeks hard work and good
fortune.

WE WILL MASTER THIS SHIT. Don't ever think otherwise dude. We all have your back.

author: Michal238
text:
Thank you guys for posting, I really appreciate it.

I also made some demo trading for me too, trying to work on patience.

That is an impressive statement .
 You are right patience and trade selection is key in this game. It is
easy to lose perspective, especially when trading on small accounts. But
 account size doesn't really matter, all that matters is % gain, and 1%
profit can be a big amount of money in the future when the account has
grown into something bigger. All we have to do is to be patient and
wait. Easier said than done, of course

As it goes for profit potential it is really hard to say, it seems to me
 that with good RTM style analysis and maxed out performance skills even
 a small account can be quite quickly multiplied to amounts of money
that is way bigger than I will ever need.

But we don't even have to think about profits and %gain. It is really
hard not to think about it but the truth is that we cannot control the
market and amount of opportunities that show up. We can control however
our routine, and how we do trading tasks. So, if we put all of our focus
 on these things then the greatest possible result will be achieved.

I have a lot of ideas on how to improve performance and all that needs
to be done now is to patiently implement them one by one instead of
trying to do it all at once - that is what I have been doing last year
and I failed. So in between posting setups, trades etc. I'll be
describing here one idea of improving performance, then I will build a
positive habit around it by excessive repetition, and go to the next
one. This process will be repeated many times until there are no things
left to improve. Its a long way ahead of me

author: Michal238
text:
I have currently one trade open on eurusd, that I didn't explain in my
 last post. It is a nice example of continuation trade. I noticed some
time ago that there are a lot of continuation opportunities after
breaking QM levels. And there is a good reason for that so this setup
gives me a nice opportunity to elaborate on that.

I try to look at price more in terms of orders opened by ITs. So at this
 point, we can say that there was a quasimodo, and then more shorts were
 opened on the way down (see my last post). The idea for continuation or
 at least bounce from broken QM lvl seems logical to me. Because I ask
myself this - what needs to happen for QM lvl to be broken? We know that
 people get trapped and orders remain at the level - in this case, buy
orders. If ITs want to push the price down they need to sell against buy
 orders. So they have shorts orders open at the level. If price goes
above this price level then it means that they will get into drawdown on
 these positions. They don't want drawdown, so they will protect this
level by adding shorts and pushing price down.

There are also other things to consider, for example - had ITs have a
chance to reverse positions already? or is there a better place for
retrace? You can see on my chart that there is no obvious better place
for retrace (CP).

This eurusd chart is beautiful, setups are rarely this clean. Its still
possible that I am wrong of course. But thinking about orders in this
way will allow for great trades when your read is correct.

So what I learned is that compression is a great indicator of where you
can expect short retrace. Sometimes price moves from a target area, and
didn't reach the opposite target, and there is "no space" for deep
retraces - so you can get in on the move on short RT.

author: Michal238
text:
I took a lot of trades this week, too much to post in real time so I'm
 going to post them in bulk. As I go forward with this journal I'll work
 on reducing the number of entries and posting them more often. I
unintentionally developed a habit of entering many times with small lots
 instead of picking one entry point. There are a lot of reasons for
that, for example:

- entering before FL (fear of missing out), and then adding more when the price gets closer to MPL

- being afraid to enter with full risk before price reacts to a level
and. Seeing price bounce gives me a feeling of being correct, so I
enter. But this feeling is not really based on my knowledge. We need to anticipate and not react
 to what price is doing. So the best moment to buy is before any signs
of price rising occur, and same goes for shorts. I think that most of
traders experience this - when the price is moving up it feels like it
will countinue, and vice versa. Sometimes even direction of the last M1
 candle influences how I feel about my trade. I need to learn to ignore
this feeling.

- not being prepared for entry beforehand. When this happens I see price
 reacting to something, then I do analysis, I find out that price is
reacting to a MPL of some important level and then I try to enter

I think that using only pending orders is the way to go. Using
pending orders means that I was prepared for entry and I anticipate what
 will happen, and I was completely prepared with my analysis beforehand
instead of reacting to what price is currently doing.

Here is my statement. This week was a fail, biggest drawdown so far. But
 it shed some light at biggest mistakes that I make in trading.

Last week only:

So, as you can see at the beginning of the week I had a lot of winners
and I took partial profits regularly. But then after a couple of losers
instead of trading the bounces, I tried to catch swings and holding
trades until it hits final TP to make up for losses. Trying to catch a
swing is probably the biggest mistakes I make in trading. And it happens
 because I try to recover from losses. Of course, it doesn't happen and I
 only lose more. This happens when I am strongly convinced that price
didn't hit the TG yet, and I am often right, but the problem with
catching swings is that:

- I ignore good entry points - because I don't want to miss the obvious move

- I don't take partial profits

- I move my stops because there is still valid engulf signal that didn't play out yet or I enter soon after being stopped out

- I don't wait for deepest possible RT

This big drawdown is the result of doing that on two correlated pairs at the same time, and this was a break of MM rules.

The red circle is where I took the biggest loss - I not only moved my SL
 but also added at the next level. Around the same time, I was trying to
 catch a move on GU, and I lost a lot. I am still convicted that EU and
GU will go down, I will write why in my next post with the trades that I
 have currently open.

It was okay to short EU, but I did it incorrectly. I didn't wait for
best prices with my entries and I didn't take partial TPs. Look at these
 left shoulder levels, and how embarrassing my trades look now:

The correct way to trade is to take touch trades in direction of the
trend, and the trend is down on EU (because it is coming from a valid
level and TG for shorts is not hit yet). Entry from PO, then TP1 after
the bounce at 1-2R, so that after SL overall result is small profit or
BE.

So the goal for next week is put more time into analyzing charts in the
evening and in the morning and finding places where I can set POs. I'll enter only from POs and take TP1 after the bounce. If I failed to take TP1 after the bounce, I'll close my trade at BE.

author: staurum
text:
I kinda agree with Edge. Noticed that i think FTR concept has "shifted" a little.

If the question is whether or not any of the boxes is FTR, then we gotta
 zoom in LTF to see where the break occurs and the deepest retrace
point, and the whole zone would be our FTR box. Up until, it reaches the
 target of the break on the left, which should be another FL on the same
 scale; then the FTR box is our FL.

If the question is whether or not this box can be trade-able, I would
wait until the break reach a target so activate the box as "FL", then we
 will have a clear PAZ to trade.
